q: The Borel density theorem (for lattices) states that if Γ is a lattice in a connected semisimple Lie group G with no compact factors, then for any representation ρ: G → GL(n,ℝ):
opts: ρ(Γ) is a lattice in ρ(G)
ρ(Γ) is Zariski-dense in ρ(G) — the closure of ρ(Γ) in the Zariski topology is all of ρ(G)
ρ restricted to Γ is trivial
exp: Borel density theorem: Γ is Zariski dense in G (when G has no compact factors). This means there are no algebraic subgroups of G strictly between Γ and G. It is used in Margulis's proof to force a homomorphism Γ → H to extend to G.
